Front: What are the three variables in GPU planning for fine-tuning?
Back: (1) Model size — determines memory floor; (2) Method — Full SFT vs LoRA vs QLoRA, determines compute multiplier; (3) Dataset scale — determines wall-clock time.

Front: What is the core trade-off between Full SFT and QLoRA?
Back: Full SFT gives maximum quality but costs 8-50x more than QLoRA. QLoRA closes 95% of the quality gap for 95% of workloads.

Front: What is QLoRA and why is it dominant for production fine-tuning?
Back: QLoRA (Quantized LoRA): fine-tunes 4-bit quantized models with low-rank adapters. Dominant because it enables fine-tuning up to 70B on a single A100-80GB with 8-50x cost reduction vs Full SFT.

Front: What is FSDP + QLoRA and what did it enable?
Back: Answer.ai (Mar 2024): Distributed QLoRA across consumer GPUs using Fully Sharded Data Parallelism. Enabled 70B fine-tuning on 2x RTX 3090 at $0.60/hr — democratizing large model fine-tuning.

Front: When should you choose QLoRA vs LoRA vs Full SFT?
Back: QLoRA: budget-constrained, <5% quality gap acceptable. LoRA: need more capacity (rank >64), quality-sensitive. Full SFT: QLoRA/LoRA leave >5% gap, have 8+ GPUs, domain radically different from pre-training.

Front: What is the "killer framing" for fine-tuning cost?
Back: Fine-tuning cost scales linearly with model size and dataset tokens. The method choice (Full/LoRA/QLoRA) provides a 10-50x cost lever without proportional quality loss.

Front: What is the cost to fine-tune Llama 3.1 70B on 10K examples?
Back: $20-60 with QLoRA (self-managed) or ~$180 via managed API.

Front: What is the memory budget formula for Full SFT?
Back: Full SFT memory = 18 * P bytes (FP16 weights + FP32 optimizer states + gradients), where P = total parameters.

Front: What is the memory budget formula for LoRA?
Back: LoRA memory = 2 * P bytes (frozen FP16 weights) + 18 * P_trainable bytes (trainable LoRA parameters with optimizer). P_trainable is typically 0.1-2% of P.

Front: What is the memory budget formula for QLoRA?
Back: QLoRA memory = 0.5 * P bytes (4-bit quantized weights) + 18 * P_trainable bytes (trainable LoRA parameters with optimizer). P_trainable is typically 0.1-2% of P.

Front: What is the formula for estimating GPU hours for a fine-tuning job?
Back: Training Time = 6 * P * D / tau, where P = parameters, D = total tokens processed, tau = number of GPUs * FLOP/s per GPU. The 6 comes from forward + backward pass cost (6 FLOPs per parameter per token).

Front: What practical throughput (tau) do A100 and H100 achieve for fine-tuning?
Back: A100 achieves ~150 TFLOP/s with Flash Attention. H100 achieves ~350 TFLOP/s.

Front: Why isn't LoRA 100x faster if it trains 100x fewer parameters?
Back: The forward pass reads ALL weights regardless of which are trainable. The backward pass is fast (only trainable params), but forward pass dominates runtime. LoRA's real advantage is memory: smaller optimizer state -> larger batches -> better GPU utilization -> 2-4x throughput gain.

Front: What is the decision tree for escalating from QLoRA to Full SFT?
Back: 1. Start QLoRA r=16, evaluate. 2. If gap >3%: increase to r=64, add FFN layers. 3. If still >3%: switch to LoRA 16-bit, r=64-128. 4. If still >5%: Full SFT (implies domain very far from pre-training).

Front: What percentage of production fine-tuning uses QLoRA or LoRA vs Full SFT?
Back: 90%+ uses QLoRA or LoRA. Full SFT is reserved for: (a) pre-training continuation, (b) safety alignment, (c) radically new modalities.

Front: What did the original LoRA paper show about rank requirements?
Back: Hu et al. (2021) showed r=8 on GPT-3 175B matched full fine-tuning quality — demonstrating that the intrinsic dimensionality of adaptation is much lower than model dimension.

Front: How does domain distance affect required LoRA rank?
Back: For domains well-represented in pre-training: r=4-16 suffices. For novel domains: r=128+ may be needed, approaching Full SFT compute.

Front: How does sequence length affect fine-tuning cost with vs without Flash Attention?
Back: With Flash Attention: cost scales linearly (2x seq = ~2x time + ~2x memory). Without Flash Attention: quadratic (2x seq = ~4x time) because the full attention matrix is materialized.

Front: What is Flash Attention and why does it matter for fine-tuning?
Back: Dao et al. (2022): Fast and memory-efficient exact attention that avoids materializing the full attention matrix. Achieves near-linear scaling with sequence length and enables longer contexts in memory-constrained settings.

Front: What is the memory impact of 128K sequence length on a 70B model?
Back: KV cache alone is ~10GB per sequence, limiting batch size to 1-2 on A100-80GB even with QLoRA. This is why long-context fine-tuning remains expensive.

Front: Is it better to fine-tune at short context and use inference-time extension (YaRN)?
Back: For most tasks, yes — fine-tune at 4-8K, serve at 128K with YaRN. Exception: if the task requires reasoning over information at specific long-range positions (e.g., document comparison), you need to fine-tune at the target length.

What is the break-even point between managed API and self-managed QLoRA?
Back: At ~5 fine-tuning runs/month on 70B, self-managed QLoRA becomes cheaper. At 50+ runs/month, self-managed saves 60-80%.

Front: What is Unsloth and what performance gains does it provide?
Back: Kernel-level optimizations for single-GPU fine-tuning that achieve 2x speed and 70% less memory without quality loss. Dominant tool for single-GPU fine-tuning workflows.

Front: What is the "rank selection" open problem in LoRA?
Back: No reliable formula exists for choosing optimal LoRA rank a priori. Empirical sweep is still required — practitioners try r=8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and pick based on eval performance.

Front: What is the MoE fine-tuning problem?
Back: Expert routing disruption during fine-tuning is poorly understood. Fine-tuning can degrade the router's learned dispatch patterns. ESFT (Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning) is promising but not mainstream.

Front: What is ESFT and what problem does it solve?
Back: Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning (Xu et al., 2024): Fine-tunes only specific experts in MoE models without disrupting the routing mechanism — enabling domain adaptation of MoE without degrading other capabilities.

Front: What is catastrophic forgetting in the context of fine-tuning?
Back: Even LoRA can degrade base model capabilities on sufficiently different domains. The model "forgets" pre-training knowledge as it adapts to new domain data.

Front: What is the replay mixing technique and when should you use it?
Back: Mix 20-30% base-task data with domain data during fine-tuning. Use when catastrophic forgetting is detected — maintains base capabilities while adapting to new domain.

Front: What is rank scheduling in LoRA fine-tuning?
Back: Start with low rank (r=8) and increase to high rank (r=64) during training. Addresses underfitting at low rank while avoiding early overfitting — progressive capacity increase.

Front: What are the 7 steps in the Design Flow Framework for fine-tuning?
Back: 1. Clarify requirements (quality bar, domain distance). 2. Identify constraints (GPU budget, timeline). 3. Propose baseline (QLoRA r=16). 4. Identify gaps (quality delta). 5. Introduce improvements (rank scaling, data quality). 6. Add evaluation (domain + regression). 7. Scaling tradeoffs.

Front: What two evaluations should you always track during fine-tuning?
Back: (1) Domain performance — how well the model performs on the target task (held-out eval set). (2) Base capability regression — whether pre-training capabilities have degraded (detect catastrophic forgetting).

Front: What is the difference between domain adaptation and capability injection?
Back: Domain adaptation: model applies existing knowledge to new domain (LoRA usually sufficient, e.g., medical language). Capability injection: model needs fundamentally new behaviors (may require Full SFT, e.g., new modality).

Front: What is DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 and when is it needed?
Back: Distributed training strategy that shards model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across GPUs. Needed for Full SFT when model doesn't fit on a single GPU or when LoRA rank is insufficient for complex domain adaptation.

Front: How does cloud GPU pricing compare across providers (June 2026)?
Back: RTX 4090: $0.50-0.69/hr. A100 80GB: $1.10-1.50/hr. H100 80GB: $2.89-3.29/hr. GCP Spot tends cheapest for A100; RunPod competitive for H100.

Front: What is the "Staff vs Principal" distinction on GPU requirements?
Back: Staff: "We need 8x H100 to fine-tune 70B." Principal: "QLoRA fits 70B on 1x A100. Start there — escalate hardware only when quality demands it." Start minimal, escalate with evidence.

Front: What is the "Staff vs Principal" distinction on data quantity?
Back: Staff: "We need more data to improve quality." Principal: "Beyond 4 epochs of repetition, adding data provides diminishing returns. Filter for quality first."

Front: What is the "Staff vs Principal" distinction on Full SFT quality?
Back: Staff: "Full fine-tuning gives best quality." Principal: "Full SFT gives 1-3% over LoRA in most domains at 10-50x cost. Measure the gap first before committing resources."

Front: What wall-clock time does QLoRA vs managed API take for 70B on 10K examples?
Back: QLoRA self-managed: 12-30 hours. Managed API: ~2-4 hours. Managed APIs are faster because providers use optimized infrastructure and parallelism.

Front: At what dataset scale should you consider FSDP multi-node?
Back: At 100K+ examples. At 1M+ examples, consider data filtering over more epochs rather than processing all data — quality filtering often gives better results than quantity.

Front: Why did H100 availability normalization matter for fine-tuning in 2025?
Back: H100 spot pricing dropped to ~$3/hr, making Full SFT of 70B economically viable for teams that need maximum quality. Previously, Full SFT was prohibitively expensive for most organizations.

Front: What is the main open problem in fine-tuning infrastructure as of 2026?
Back: Optimal rank selection for LoRA — no reliable a priori formula exists. Current practice requires empirical sweeps, adding cost and time to the fine-tuning process.

Front: How did fine-tuning shift from 2023 to 2026 in terms of default approach?
Back: From "Full SFT on clusters" to "QLoRA on single GPUs" as the default for most workloads. Fine-tuning became a commodity operation rather than an infrastructure challenge.

Front: What is the typical speedup from LoRA/QLoRA vs Full SFT in practice?
Back: 2-4x speedup (NOT proportional to the 100-1000x reduction in trainable parameters). The savings come from memory reduction enabling larger batch sizes, not from reduced forward-pass computation.

Front: What is the three-layer architecture of a fine-tuning pipeline?
Back: (1) Data Layer: dataset prep + filtering. (2) Compute Layer: method router (Full/LoRA/QLoRA) + GPU cluster. (3) Evaluation Layer: domain eval (held-out) + base capability regression testing.

Front: What are the two GPU scaling strategies for distributed fine-tuning?
Back: FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallelism): shards model across GPUs, each processes different data. ZeRO-3 (DeepSpeed): shards parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across GPUs. Both enable training models that don't fit on a single GPU.

Front: What determines whether sequence length or parameter count is the memory bottleneck?
Back: For short sequences (<4K) on large models: parameter count dominates. For long sequences (128K+): KV cache and activations dominate, regardless of model size, limiting batch size severely.

Front: What does the Muennighoff et al. (2023) paper on scaling data-constrained LMs show?
Back: Provides guidance on how to effectively train when data is limited — showing diminishing returns from repeated epochs and establishing principles for data-constrained training.

Front: What is the Full SFT cost for a 405B model on 10K examples?
Back: $10,000-40,000 for self-managed, ~$1,000 via managed API. This makes managed APIs especially cost-effective for very large models.
